paragraphs: The Discovery V8 was fitted to the first two generations of the Discovery — the D1 (1989–1998) and the D2 (1998–2004). Both used the same AJ41 petrol V8, offered in 3.9-litre form in the earlier cars and 4.0-litre in the later ones. It was the petrol flagship of the range during that era, sitting alongside the Tdi and Td5 diesel variants. The Discovery V8 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road. Land Rover Discovery V8 Engine Codes AJ41 (D1/L318, D2/L318 facelift) A 3.9-litre (D1) or 4.0-litre (D2) V8 petrol engine fitted to the Discovery from 1989 to 2004. No widely-reported engine issue for this variant — we still recommend a full inspection before any long journey. We replace timing chains, valve seals, coolant components, and bearings as standard on every rebuild. Check Your AJ41 Discovery V8 → [link to quote form] Land Rover Discovery V8 Engine Compatibility The AJ41 V8 in the Discovery is a straightforward fitment across the D1 and D2 generations, but the capacity changed from 3.9 litres to 4.0 litres partway through production. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (AJ41) and capacity via registration or VIN - Your generation (D1/L318 or D2/L318 facelift) - Drivetrain and ancillary specification - Any ECU or emissions considerations specific to your exact build This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Discovery V8 quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the Discovery V8 from 2023 to present. The engine features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older engine V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every engine rebuild.
